git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The gastro-esophageal junction lies at which vertebral level?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The esophagus pierces the diaphragm and joins the stomach at approximately T10.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which artery is the primary blood supply to the greater curvature of the stomach?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The right and left gastroepiploic arteries run along the greater curvature.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The ligament of Treitz marks the junction between which two structures?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The suspensory ligament of Treitz marks the duodenojejunal flexure.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which part of the duodenum is retroperitoneal?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The D2-D4 segments of the duodenum are secondarily retroperitoneal; D1 is mostly intraperitoneal.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The portal vein is formed by the union of which two veins?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The portal vein forms behind the neck of the pancreas from the splenic and superior mesenteric veins.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which structure passes through the epiploic foramen (of Winslow)?
o: The portal triad borders it but nothing passes through its opening except as a communication route
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The epiploic foramen is a communication between the greater and lesser sacs, bordered anteriorly by the portal triad.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The appendix is most commonly located in which position relative to the cecum?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The retrocecal position is the most common anatomical position of the vermiform appendix.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: McBurney's point is located at the junction of which two landmarks?
o: Lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of a line from the ASIS to the umbilicus
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: McBurney's point overlies the base of the appendix in most individuals.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which ligament connects the liver to the anterior abdominal wall?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The falciform ligament attaches the liver to the anterior abdominal wall and diaphragm.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The porta hepatis transmits which three structures?
o: Hepatic veins, portal vein, bile duct
Hepatic artery, hepatic veins, common bile duct
Hepatic artery, portal vein, common bile duct
Portal vein, IVC, common bile duct
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The portal triad (hepatic artery proper, portal vein, common bile duct) enters/exits at the porta hepatis.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The gallbladder's fundus typically projects at which surface landmark?
o: Midclavicular line at the costal margin (tip of 9th costal cartilage)
Right lumbar region at the iliac crest
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The gallbladder fundus lies where the right midclavicular line meets the costal margin.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Calot's triangle is bounded by the cystic duct, common hepatic duct, and which structure?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Calot's (cystohepatic) triangle is bounded by the cystic duct, common hepatic duct, and inferior liver surface; the cystic artery is typically found within it.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The head of the pancreas is encircled by which structure?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The C-shaped curve of the duodenum wraps around the pancreatic head.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The main pancreatic duct (of Wirsung) typically joins the common bile duct to form which structure?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The main pancreatic duct joins the CBD to form the hepatopancreatic ampulla (ampulla of Vater), opening at the major duodenal papilla.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which segment of the colon is retroperitoneal on both its ascending and descending portions?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The ascending and descending colon are secondarily retroperitoneal; the transverse and sigmoid colon are intraperitoneal (mobile).

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The marginal artery of Drummond connects branches of which two arteries?
o: Celiac trunk and superior mesenteric artery
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The marginal artery provides a continuous anastomotic arcade linking the SMA and IMA territories along the colon.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The rectum receives its blood supply mainly from branches of which vessel(s)?
o: Superior, middle, and inferior rectal arteries
Only the internal iliac artery directly
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The rectum has a dual/triple supply from the superior (IMA), middle (internal iliac), and inferior (internal pudendal) rectal arteries.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The dentate (pectinate) line marks the transition between which two epithelial types in the anal canal?
o: Simple columnar above to stratified squamous below
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Above the dentate line the anal canal is lined by columnar epithelium (endodermal origin); below it, stratified squamous epithelium (ectodermal origin).

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which nerve provides sensory innervation above the dentate line versus below it?
o: Both are supplied equally by autonomic fibers
Above: autonomic (visceral) fibers, insensitive to pain; below: pudendal nerve (somatic), pain-sensitive
Above: pudendal nerve; below: autonomic fibers
Both above and below are supplied by the pudendal nerve
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: This explains why internal hemorrhoids (above the line) are painless while external hemorrhoids (below) are painful.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The lesser omentum extends between the liver and which two structures?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The lesser omentum (hepatogastric and hepatoduodenal ligaments) connects the liver to the lesser curvature of the stomach and the duodenum.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Portal hypertension leads to esophageal varices due to anastomosis between the left gastric vein and which vein?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Portosystemic anastomosis occurs between the left gastric (portal) and esophageal veins draining into the azygos (systemic) system.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The greater omentum develops embryologically from which structure?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The greater omentum derives from the dorsal mesogastrium, which grows down to form the omental apron.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Meckel's diverticulum is a remnant of which embryological structure?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Meckel's diverticulum results from incomplete obliteration of the vitelline duct.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: By the 'rule of twos,' Meckel's diverticulum is typically located how far from the ileocecal valve?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The classic rule of twos states it is found about 2 feet from the ileocecal valve, is 2 inches long, and occurs in 2% of the population.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which peritoneal recess is the most common site for internal herniation and the most dependent part of the peritoneal cavity in a supine patient?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Morison's pouch (hepatorenal recess) is the most dependent part of the peritoneal cavity in a supine person.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The inferior mesenteric artery supplies which portion of the gut?
o: Hindgut (distal one-third of transverse colon to upper rectum)
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The IMA is the artery of the hindgut, from the distal transverse colon to the upper rectum.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which structure marks the boundary between the foregut and midgut in blood supply terms?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The foregut-midgut boundary is at the level of the second part of the duodenum, near the major duodenal papilla.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The spleen lies deep to which ribs on the left side?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The spleen normally lies beneath the 9th to 11th ribs in the left hypochondrium.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which ligament connects the spleen to the stomach and transmits the short gastric vessels?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The gastrosplenic ligament carries the short gastric and left gastroepiploic vessels.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The hepatorenal recess and phrenicocolic ligament are anatomically important because they can limit the spread of infection to which structure?
o: Spleen via the phrenicocolic ligament acting as a shelf
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The phrenicocolic ligament forms a shelf that supports the spleen and can limit fluid tracking to the left paracolic gutter.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which layer of the gut wall contains the myenteric (Auerbach's) plexus?
o: Between the inner circular and outer longitudinal muscle layers
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Auerbach's plexus lies between the two muscularis externa layers and primarily controls motility.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which layer contains the submucosal (Meissner's) plexus?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Meissner's plexus lies within the submucosa and regulates secretion and local blood flow.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The falciform ligament contains which remnant structure in adults?
o: Ligamentum teres hepatis (remnant of umbilical vein)
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The ligamentum teres, a fibrous remnant of the fetal umbilical vein, runs in the free edge of the falciform ligament.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which segment of Couinaud's liver segmentation corresponds to the caudate lobe?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Segment I corresponds to the caudate lobe in the Couinaud classification.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The transpyloric plane (of Addison) at L1 vertebral level corresponds to which structure?
o: Pylorus of the stomach and neck of the pancreas
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The transpyloric plane at L1 passes through the pylorus, the pancreatic neck, and the hila of the kidneys.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which nerve is at risk during appendectomy, and its injury may weaken the abdominal wall?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The ilioinguinal nerve runs near the appendix incision site and can be inadvertently injured.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: The greater curvature of the stomach gives attachment to which two omenta/ligaments?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The greater omentum and gastrosplenic ligament both attach along the greater curvature.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Which structure is a landmark for locating the ileocecal junction, receiving the terminal ileum?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The ileocecal valve marks the junction where the terminal ileum opens into the cecum.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: During embryological rotation, the midgut undergoes rotation around the axis of which artery?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: The midgut rotates 270 degrees counterclockwise around the SMA axis during development.

git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.s: Failure of midgut rotation to complete normally, with the cecum remaining in the right upper quadrant and abnormal peritoneal (Ladd's) bands, describes which condition?
git-and-nutrition/git-anatomy.e: Intestinal malrotation results from incomplete rotation and fixation of the midgut, predisposing to volvulus.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which cell type in the gastric mucosa secretes hydrochloric acid?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Parietal cells secrete both hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which hormone, released from G cells, is the primary stimulus for gastric acid secretion?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Gastrin stimulates parietal cells directly and via histamine release from ECL cells.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Intrinsic factor, essential for vitamin B12 absorption, is secreted by which cells?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Parietal cells secrete intrinsic factor, which binds B12 for absorption in the terminal ileum.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which phase of gastric secretion is mediated primarily by the sight, smell, and thought of food?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The cephalic phase is triggered by sensory stimuli acting via the vagus nerve before food reaches the stomach.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Secretin is released from S cells of the duodenum in response to which stimulus?
o: Acidic chyme (low pH) entering the duodenum
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Secretin release is triggered by acid in the duodenum, stimulating pancreatic bicarbonate secretion.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Cholecystokinin (CCK) is released in response to which luminal content and causes what effect?
o: Fatty acids and amino acids; stimulates gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: CCK responds to fats and proteins, causing gallbladder contraction and pancreatic acinar enzyme secretion.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which pancreatic enzyme is secreted in its active form, unlike most other pancreatic proteases?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Pancreatic amylase and lipase are secreted in active form; the proteases are secreted as inactive zymogens.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Trypsinogen is activated to trypsin by which enzyme on the duodenal brush border?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Enterokinase cleaves trypsinogen to active trypsin, which then activates other zymogens.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Bile salts aid fat digestion primarily through which mechanism?
o: Emulsification, increasing surface area for lipase action
Direct absorption of fats into enterocytes
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Bile salts emulsify fats into smaller droplets and form micelles, facilitating lipase action and absorption.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which segment of the small intestine is the primary site for vitamin B12-intrinsic factor complex absorption?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The B12-intrinsic factor complex is absorbed by specific receptors in the terminal ileum.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Bile salts are reabsorbed and recycled primarily through which process?
o: Passive diffusion throughout the small intestine
Enterohepatic circulation via active transport in the terminal ileum
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Approximately 95% of bile salts undergo enterohepatic circulation, reabsorbed actively in the terminal ileum.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which type of intestinal contraction mixes chyme without significant net forward movement?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Segmentation contractions mix and expose chyme to the mucosa without substantial aboral propulsion.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: The migrating motor complex (MMC) primarily functions to do what during the fasting state?
o: Sweep undigested debris and bacteria through the GI tract
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The MMC is a housekeeping motility pattern occurring between meals, cleared by motilin.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which hormone is primarily responsible for initiating the migrating motor complex?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Motilin, released during fasting, triggers the MMC.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Gastric emptying of liquids follows what general pattern compared to solids?
o: Liquids are not affected by osmolarity
Both empty at the same rate
Liquids empty faster than solids, generally following first-order kinetics
Solids are never retained in the stomach
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Liquids generally empty faster and more predictably; solids require trituration before emptying.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which reflex slows gastric emptying when fat-rich or hyperosmolar chyme enters the duodenum?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The enterogastric reflex, mediated via CCK, secretin, and neural pathways, slows gastric emptying to protect the duodenum.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which digestive enzyme in saliva begins carbohydrate digestion in the mouth?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Salivary amylase begins starch digestion, though its action is limited by gastric acid inactivation.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Pepsinogen is converted to active pepsin by which mechanism?
o: Gastric acid (autocatalytically once some pepsin is formed)
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Low gastric pH converts pepsinogen to pepsin, which then autocatalytically activates more pepsinogen.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which brush-border enzyme is responsible for the final digestion step of disaccharides such as lactose?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Lactase on the brush border hydrolyzes lactose into glucose and galactose.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Glucose and galactose are absorbed into enterocytes primarily via which transporter?
o: GLUT2 only at the apical membrane
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: SGLT1 cotransports glucose/galactose with sodium across the apical membrane.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Fructose is absorbed into enterocytes primarily via which transporter?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Fructose absorption occurs via facilitated diffusion through GLUT5, independent of sodium.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Long-chain fatty acids are absorbed into enterocytes and re-esterified before being packaged into which structure for lymphatic transport?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Long-chain fatty acids are re-esterified into triglycerides and packaged into chylomicrons, absorbed via lacteals.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which vitamin's absorption is most dependent on bile salt micelle formation?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Fat-soluble vitamins require micellar solubilization by bile salts for efficient absorption.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Iron absorption occurs predominantly in which part of the small intestine and in which form is it best absorbed?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Iron is absorbed mainly in the duodenum, and the ferrous (Fe2+) form is more readily absorbed than ferric (Fe3+).

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which hormone regulates systemic iron absorption by controlling ferroportin degradation?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Hepcidin, produced by the liver, downregulates ferroportin, reducing iron release from enterocytes into plasma.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which of the following best describes the primary function of gastric mucus and bicarbonate secretion?
o: Protecting gastric mucosa from acid and pepsin (mucus-bicarbonate barrier)
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The mucus-bicarbonate layer protects the gastric epithelium from autodigestion.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which prostaglandin plays a key protective role in gastric mucosal defense?
o: Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), which stimulates mucus and bicarbonate secretion
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: PGE2 enhances mucosal blood flow, mucus, and bicarbonate secretion, protecting against ulceration; NSAIDs impair this via COX inhibition.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: The gastrocolic reflex describes which physiological response?
o: Food entering the stomach triggering increased colonic motility and mass movements
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The gastrocolic reflex increases colonic motility in response to gastric filling, often leading to a post-meal urge to defecate.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which ion channel/transporter defect underlies cystic fibrosis-related pancreatic insufficiency?
o: CFTR chloride channel dysfunction, impairing bicarbonate-rich fluid secretion
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: CFTR dysfunction impairs chloride and bicarbonate secretion, leading to thick pancreatic secretions and duct obstruction.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Water absorption in the small intestine occurs primarily by which mechanism?
o: Facilitated diffusion via water channels only in the colon
Osmosis, following the absorption of solutes such as sodium and glucose
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Water absorption is largely passive, driven osmotically by solute (especially sodium and glucose) absorption.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which segment of the colon absorbs the majority of remaining water and electrolytes from chyme?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The proximal colon (ascending and transverse) is the primary site of water and electrolyte absorption.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which neurotransmitter released by enteric neurons is primarily responsible for smooth muscle relaxation (as in receptive relaxation of the stomach)?
o: Nitric oxide and vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Nitric oxide and VIP are key inhibitory neurotransmitters mediating smooth muscle relaxation in the gut.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Defecation reflex involves relaxation of which sphincter under voluntary control?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The external anal sphincter is skeletal muscle under voluntary somatic control via the pudendal nerve.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which hormone inhibits both gastric acid secretion and motility, acting as a general GI inhibitor?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Somatostatin broadly inhibits gastric secretion, motility, and the release of other GI hormones.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: The Meissner's plexus is primarily responsible for regulating which gut function?
o: Local blood flow and secretory activity of the mucosa
Skeletal muscle control of the esophagus
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: The submucosal plexus mainly governs secretion and local mucosal blood flow.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which of the following best explains why pancreatic lipase requires colipase for optimal function?
o: Colipase transports fatty acids into enterocytes
Colipase displaces bile salts from the lipid droplet surface, anchoring lipase for activity
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Bile salts alone can inhibit lipase by coating fat droplets; colipase helps anchor lipase to the lipid-water interface.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Chief cells of the gastric glands primarily secrete which substance?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen, the inactive precursor of pepsin.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which vitamin deficiency results from chronic loss of intrinsic factor, as in pernicious anemia?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Loss of intrinsic factor (due to parietal cell autoimmune destruction) impairs B12 absorption in the terminal ileum.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which stimulus directly triggers CCK-induced gallbladder contraction and relaxation of the sphincter of Oddi?
o: Fat and protein digestion products in the duodenum
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: Fatty acids and amino acids in the duodenum stimulate CCK release, causing gallbladder contraction and sphincter of Oddi relaxation.

git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.s: Which of the following gut hormones is considered an incretin, enhancing insulin secretion in response to oral glucose?
git-and-nutrition/git-physiology.e: GLP-1, released from L cells in the distal gut, potentiates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (the incretin effect).

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Bilirubin is primarily produced from the breakdown of which molecule?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Heme catabolism from senescent red cells produces biliverdin, then unconjugated bilirubin.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Unconjugated bilirubin is transported in plasma bound to which protein?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin is lipid-soluble and travels bound to albumin.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Conjugation of bilirubin in the liver is performed by which enzyme?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: UDP-glucuronyl transferase conjugates bilirubin with glucuronic acid, making it water-soluble for biliary excretion.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which enzyme deficiency causes Gilbert syndrome, a mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia?
o: Partial reduction in UDP-glucuronyl transferase activity
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Gilbert syndrome results from mildly reduced (not absent) UDP-glucuronyl transferase activity.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Crigler-Najjar syndrome type I is characterized by which enzymatic defect?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Type I Crigler-Najjar involves complete absence of the conjugating enzyme, causing severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which of the following liver function tests is most specific for hepatocellular injury (as opposed to biliary/cholestatic disease)?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: ALT and AST are released from damaged hepatocytes, indicating hepatocellular injury.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which liver enzyme is more specific to the liver, being minimally present in other tissues, compared to AST?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: ALT is relatively liver-specific, while AST is also found in cardiac and skeletal muscle.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which coagulation factor's synthesis is a sensitive early marker of hepatic synthetic dysfunction, given its short half-life?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Factor VII has the shortest half-life of the vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, making prothrombin time an early marker of liver synthetic failure.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which plasma protein, synthesized by the liver, is most useful for assessing chronic (not acute) hepatic synthetic function?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Albumin's long half-life (about 20 days) makes it more reflective of chronic liver synthetic function rather than acute changes.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Ammonia detoxification in the liver occurs primarily via which pathway?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: The liver converts toxic ammonia into urea via the urea cycle for renal excretion.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which rate-limiting enzyme catalyzes the first committed step of the urea cycle?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase I (mitochondrial) catalyzes the first, rate-limiting step of the urea cycle.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Hepatic encephalopathy is most closely associated with elevated levels of which substance?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Impaired hepatic ammonia clearance leads to accumulation, contributing to hepatic encephalopathy.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which zone of the liver acinus is most susceptible to ischemic injury due to its distal location relative to blood supply?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Zone 3 (around the central vein) receives the least oxygenated blood and is most vulnerable to ischemia and toxin-related injury.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which zone of the liver acinus is most active in oxidative metabolic processes such as gluconeogenesis and beta-oxidation?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Zone 1 receives the most oxygenated blood and is metabolically active in oxidative pathways.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which cells within liver sinusoids function as resident macrophages?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Kupffer cells are specialized macrophages lining the hepatic sinusoids, clearing bacteria and debris.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Hepatic stellate cells (Ito cells), when activated, are primarily responsible for which pathological process?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Activated stellate cells transform into myofibroblast-like cells producing excess collagen, driving liver fibrosis/cirrhosis.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Bile is composed primarily of which four components?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Bile's major organic components are bile salts, bilirubin, cholesterol, and phospholipids, along with water and electrolytes.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Gallstone formation due to excess cholesterol relative to bile salts and lecithin describes which mechanism?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Cholesterol gallstones form when bile becomes supersaturated with cholesterol relative to solubilizing bile salts and lecithin.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Black pigment gallstones are most commonly associated with which underlying condition?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Chronic hemolytic conditions increase unconjugated bilirubin, predisposing to black pigment stones.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Acute pancreatitis is most commonly caused by which two etiologies?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Gallstones and alcohol use account for the large majority of acute pancreatitis cases.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which laboratory enzyme is most specific for diagnosing acute pancreatitis?
o: Lipase (more specific and remains elevated longer)
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Serum lipase is more specific to the pancreas than amylase and remains elevated for a longer period.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Autodigestion of the pancreas in acute pancreatitis primarily results from premature activation of which enzyme within the gland?
o: Trypsinogen to trypsin within acinar cells
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Premature intra-pancreatic activation of trypsinogen to trypsin triggers a cascade activating other proenzymes, causing autodigestion.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency, as in chronic pancreatitis, most directly leads to malabsorption of which nutrient class?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Loss of pancreatic lipase causes fat malabsorption and steatorrhea, along with fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which pancreatic islet cell type secretes glucagon?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Alpha cells of the islets of Langerhans secrete glucagon in response to hypoglycemia.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Insulin is synthesized as a precursor called proinsulin, which is cleaved to form insulin and which byproduct?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Cleavage of proinsulin yields insulin and C-peptide in equimolar amounts, useful for assessing endogenous insulin production.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which hormone, secreted by delta cells of the pancreas, inhibits both insulin and glucagon secretion?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Somatostatin exerts paracrine inhibitory control over neighboring islet cells.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Portal hypertension is most commonly caused by which condition?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Cirrhosis causes increased intrahepatic resistance to portal flow, the most common cause of portal hypertension.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which of the following is a recognized clinical sign of portal hypertension?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Portosystemic collateral formation manifests as esophageal varices, caput medusae, and splenomegaly due to congestion.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Hepatitis B virus is primarily transmitted via which route?
o: Blood and body fluids (parenteral, sexual, perinatal)
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: HBV spreads through blood and body fluid exposure, unlike hepatitis A and E which are fecal-oral.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which hepatitis virus is most associated with fecal-oral transmission and typically causes a self-limited acute illness without chronicity?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Hepatitis A is fecal-oral transmitted and does not cause chronic infection.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which serologic marker indicates current hepatitis B infection and infectivity?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: HBsAg positivity indicates active infection (acute or chronic) and potential infectivity.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Wilson's disease results from abnormal accumulation of which metal due to impaired biliary excretion?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Wilson's disease is caused by mutations in the ATP7B gene, impairing copper transport and excretion into bile.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Hereditary hemochromatosis results in excess accumulation of which substance, often affecting the liver, heart, and pancreas?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Hemochromatosis causes excess intestinal iron absorption and deposition in multiple organs.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which vitamin deficiency is most likely in a patient with long-standing obstructive jaundice and fat malabsorption, presenting with a bleeding tendency?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Vitamin K is fat-soluble and required for synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X; its malabsorption in cholestasis causes coagulopathy.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: The first-pass effect refers to which pharmacokinetic phenomenon relevant to the liver?
o: Excretion of a drug unchanged in bile
Rapid renal excretion of a drug before absorption
Hepatic metabolism of an orally absorbed drug before it reaches systemic circulation
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Orally absorbed drugs pass through the portal circulation to the liver first, where significant metabolism may occur before systemic distribution.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which of the following best describes the function of gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) in liver disease evaluation?
o: Sensitive but non-specific marker of biliary/cholestatic disease and alcohol use
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: GGT rises in cholestatic liver disease and with alcohol use but lacks specificity on its own.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which of the following pancreatic hormones raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Glucagon, secreted during fasting/hypoglycemia, raises blood glucose via hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: The gallbladder concentrates bile primarily by absorbing which substance from stored bile?
o: Water and electrolytes (mainly sodium and chloride)
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: The gallbladder epithelium actively reabsorbs sodium (with water following), concentrating bile up to tenfold.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Courvoisier's law relates a palpable, non-tender, distended gallbladder with painless jaundice to which likely underlying cause?
o: Malignant obstruction of the common bile duct (e.g., pancreatic head cancer)
Acute cholecystitis due to gallstone impaction
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: Courvoisier's law suggests malignant obstruction (rather than stones, which usually cause a fibrotic, non-distensible gallbladder) when a palpable gallbladder accompanies painless jaundice.

git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.s: Which of the following is the primary rate-limiting enzyme for hepatic cholesterol synthesis, targeted by statin drugs?
git-and-nutrition/liver-gallbladder-and-.e: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the rate-limiting step of cholesterol biosynthesis and is inhibited by statins.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which layer of the gut wall is responsible for peristaltic movement through its two smooth muscle layers?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The muscularis externa, with inner circular and outer longitudinal layers, generates peristalsis.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The esophagus is lined by which type of epithelium?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The esophagus has a protective stratified squamous non-keratinized epithelium suited to withstand abrasion from food.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Gastric pits lead into glands lined by which combination of specialized cells in the body/fundus of the stomach?
o: Parietal, chief, and mucous neck cells
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Fundic/body gastric glands contain parietal, chief, and mucous neck cells, along with enteroendocrine cells.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which specialized epithelial cells, unique to the small intestine, secrete antimicrobial substances such as lysozyme and defensins?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Paneth cells, located at the base of intestinal crypts, secrete antimicrobial peptides contributing to innate mucosal defense.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which specialized cells overlying Peyer's patches sample luminal antigens for immune surveillance?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: M cells transport antigens and microorganisms from the gut lumen to underlying immune cells in Peyer's patches.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The finger-like projections increasing surface area in the small intestine, visible on light microscopy, are called what?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Villi are macroscopic/microscopic projections of mucosa and submucosa that increase small intestinal absorptive surface area.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Plicae circulares (valves of Kerckring) are permanent circular folds found predominantly in which part of the small intestine?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Plicae circulares are most developed in the distal duodenum and jejunum, decreasing distally in the ileum.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which histological feature is unique to the large intestine, distinguishing it from the small intestine, aside from the absence of villi?
o: Abundant goblet cells and no villi
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The colon lacks villi and has abundant goblet cells within straight crypts of Lieberkuhn for mucus secretion, aiding stool passage.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Brunner's glands, which secrete alkaline mucus to neutralize gastric acid, are located in which part of the GI tract?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Brunner's glands are a distinguishing histological feature of the duodenal submucosa.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The liver's classic lobule is organized around which central structure?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The classic hepatic lobule is a hexagonal unit with a central vein at its center and portal triads at its periphery.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Bile canaliculi are formed by which structures?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Bile canaliculi are tiny channels formed by specialized grooves in the plasma membranes of adjacent hepatocytes.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The pancreas develops embryologically from which two buds that later fuse?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The pancreas forms from fusion of dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds arising from the foregut endoderm.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Annular pancreas, a congenital anomaly causing duodenal obstruction, results from abnormal behavior of which embryological structure?
o: Absence of the dorsal bud entirely
Failure of the dorsal bud to rotate
Ventral pancreatic bud splitting and encircling the duodenum abnormally
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Annular pancreas occurs when the ventral bud bifurcates and surrounds the duodenum, potentially causing obstruction.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The liver develops embryologically as an outgrowth from which structure?
o: Septum transversum alone without endodermal contribution
Hepatic diverticulum from the foregut endoderm
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The liver bud (hepatic diverticulum) arises from foregut endoderm and grows into the septum transversum mesenchyme.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which embryological structure gives rise to both the liver parenchyma and the biliary tree?
o: Hepatic diverticulum (pars hepatica and pars cystica)
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The hepatic diverticulum divides into a cranial part (liver and hepatic ducts) and caudal part (gallbladder and cystic duct).

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Esophageal atresia with tracheoesophageal fistula most commonly results from abnormal division of which embryological structure?
o: Foregut into trachea and esophagus (tracheoesophageal septum)
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Incomplete or abnormal partitioning of the foregut into respiratory and esophageal components causes tracheoesophageal anomalies.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Congenital pyloric stenosis primarily involves hypertrophy of which structure?
o: Circular muscle layer of the pylorus
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Hypertrophic pyloric stenosis involves marked thickening of the circular smooth muscle at the pylorus, causing gastric outlet obstruction.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Hirschsprung disease results from failure of migration of which embryological cell type into the distal colon?
o: Neural crest cells (forming enteric ganglion cells)
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Absence of neural crest-derived ganglion cells in the distal bowel results in a functionally obstructed, aganglionic segment.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Omphalocele differs from gastroschisis primarily in which anatomical feature?
o: Omphalocele has a peritoneal sac covering herniated organs; gastroschisis does not
Gastroschisis occurs at the umbilical ring; omphalocele occurs lateral to it
Gastroschisis is always associated with other anomalies, omphalocele is not
Omphalocele always involves only the stomach
There is no meaningful anatomical difference
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Omphalocele involves herniation of abdominal contents into the umbilical cord covered by peritoneum/amnion; gastroschisis is an uncovered defect lateral to the umbilicus.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The greater and lesser omenta, along with the peritoneal cavity's complex folds, develop due to rotation of which embryological structure?
o: The stomach and its dorsal/ventral mesenteries
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Rotation of the stomach along with differential growth of its dorsal and ventral mesenteries creates the definitive peritoneal cavity arrangement, including the lesser sac.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which histological hallmark is characteristic of Barrett's esophagus, a metaplastic response to chronic acid reflux?
o: Replacement of columnar with squamous epithelium
Replacement of stratified squamous epithelium with columnar epithelium with goblet cells (intestinal metaplasia)
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Barrett's esophagus is defined by intestinal-type columnar metaplasia replacing the normal squamous esophageal epithelium.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which cell type in the gastric mucosa is the origin of most gastric adenocarcinomas, and metaplastic change here is a precursor lesion?
o: Surface mucous/glandular epithelial cells undergoing intestinal metaplasia
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Chronic gastritis (e.g., from H. pylori) can lead to intestinal metaplasia of gastric glandular epithelium, a recognized precursor to gastric adenocarcinoma.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The muscularis mucosae is a thin smooth muscle layer located in which part of the gut wall?
o: Between the two muscularis externa layers
Between the submucosa and muscularis externa
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The muscularis mucosae is a thin layer of smooth muscle at the boundary of the mucosa and submucosa, aiding local mucosal movement.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Peyer's patches, aggregates of lymphoid tissue, are most abundant in which part of the small intestine?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Peyer's patches are most concentrated in the lamina propria and submucosa of the terminal ileum.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which cell type of the gastric antrum secretes gastrin?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: G cells, located mainly in the gastric antrum, secrete gastrin into the bloodstream.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Enteroendocrine cells of the GI tract are part of which broader cell system, given their shared embryological origin and hormone-secreting function?
o: APUD (amine precursor uptake and decarboxylation) / diffuse neuroendocrine system
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Enteroendocrine cells belong to the diffuse neuroendocrine system, historically termed APUD cells.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which developmental defect results from incomplete recanalization of the duodenal lumen during embryogenesis?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The duodenum undergoes a solid phase followed by recanalization; failure of this process causes duodenal atresia or stenosis.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which layer of the gut wall is absent in the esophagus above the diaphragm, being replaced by adventitia instead?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The intrathoracic esophagus lacks a serosal covering, having adventitia instead, which has surgical significance for anastomotic healing.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The lamina propria of the intestinal mucosa contains which type of connective tissue and immune cells?
o: Dense regular connective tissue with no immune cells
Loose connective tissue rich in immune cells (lymphocytes, plasma cells, macrophages)
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The lamina propria is loose connective tissue containing a rich population of immune cells supporting mucosal immunity.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which structure, formed embryologically from the yolk sac connection, if it persists abnormally as a fibrous band, can cause volvulus or obstruction?
o: Vitelline duct remnant (fibrous band to the umbilicus)
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: A persistent fibrous vitelline duct remnant can act as a band around which bowel twists, causing volvulus.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which cell type lines the hepatic sinusoids, in addition to Kupffer cells, and is characterized by fenestrations allowing plasma exchange?
o: Simple squamous sinusoidal endothelial cells (fenestrated, no basement membrane)
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Hepatic sinusoidal endothelium is discontinuous and fenestrated, lacking a complete basement membrane, facilitating exchange between blood and hepatocytes.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The space of Disse, located between hepatocytes and sinusoidal endothelium, contains which important cell type involved in fibrosis?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Stellate cells reside in the space of Disse and store vitamin A normally, but transform into fibrogenic myofibroblasts when activated.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Intraepithelial lymphocytes are prominently found within which layer of the small intestinal mucosa?
o: Between the epithelial cells lining the villi
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Intraepithelial lymphocytes reside between enterocytes, contributing to mucosal immune surveillance.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which of the following best describes the histological appearance of celiac disease affecting the small intestinal mucosa?
o: Presence of granulomas throughout the mucosa
Villous atrophy with crypt hyperplasia and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes
Normal villous architecture with goblet cell hyperplasia
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Celiac disease classically shows villous blunting/atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, and increased intraepithelial lymphocytes due to gluten-triggered immune injury.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The transition from esophagus to stomach (gastroesophageal junction) shows an abrupt change from which epithelium to which?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The Z-line marks the abrupt transition from esophageal stratified squamous to gastric simple columnar epithelium.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which histological feature distinguishes the jejunum from the ileum, aside from more prominent plicae circulares?
o: Absence of muscularis externa in jejunum
More goblet cells in jejunum than ileum
Presence of Brunner's glands in jejunum
Thicker wall, longer villi, and fewer Peyer's patches in the jejunum compared to ileum
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The jejunum has a thicker wall with taller, more numerous villi and fewer Peyer's patches compared to the ileum.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Failure of the proctodeum and hindgut to properly communicate during development results in which congenital anomaly?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Imperforate anus results from abnormal development of the anorectal canal and its membrane, failing to establish a patent connection.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The cloaca is divided by the urorectal septum into which two structures?
o: Bladder and rectum directly without an intermediate structure
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The urorectal septum divides the cloaca into the ventral urogenital sinus and dorsal anorectal canal.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: Which histological layer of the stomach is thrown into folds called rugae, allowing for distension?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: Gastric rugae are formed by folding of the mucosa and submucosa, flattening out as the stomach distends with food.

git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.s: The three rotations of the midgut during embryological development total how many degrees, and in which direction?
git-and-nutrition/git-histology-and-embr.e: The midgut undergoes a total of 270 degrees of counterclockwise rotation around the SMA axis during normal development.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which macronutrient provides the highest caloric density per gram?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Fats provide approximately 9 kcal/g, more than double that of carbohydrates or proteins.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which amino acids are classified as essential, meaning they cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained from the diet?
o: Histidine, isoleucine, leucine, lysine, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, valine
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: These nine amino acids cannot be synthesized endogenously in adequate amounts and must come from dietary protein.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Kwashiorkor, a form of protein-energy malnutrition, is classically characterized by which finding?
o: Edema (due to hypoalbuminemia) despite adequate caloric intake but inadequate protein
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Kwashiorkor results from adequate calories but inadequate protein intake, causing hypoalbuminemia and edema.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Marasmus, in contrast to kwashiorkor, is characterized by which pattern of malnutrition?
o: Severe overall caloric and protein deficiency leading to significant wasting without edema
Excess protein intake with normal calories
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Marasmus results from severe overall calorie and protein deficiency, causing significant muscle and fat wasting without the edema seen in kwashiorkor.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which vitamin deficiency causes beriberi, affecting cardiovascular and nervous systems?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Thiamine deficiency causes beriberi, presenting as wet (cardiovascular) or dry (neurological) forms.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which vitamin deficiency causes pellagra, classically presenting with dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Niacin deficiency causes pellagra, the '3 D's': dermatitis, diarrhea, and dementia.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Scurvy, caused by vitamin C deficiency, results in which characteristic pathology due to impaired collagen synthesis?
o: Bleeding gums, poor wound healing, and perifollicular hemorrhages
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Vitamin C is a cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylase in collagen synthesis; deficiency impairs collagen cross-linking, causing bleeding and poor wound healing.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Vitamin A deficiency classically presents with which ocular manifestation?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Vitamin A is essential for rhodopsin synthesis in rod cells; deficiency causes night blindness and can progress to xerophthalmia.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Vitamin D deficiency in children results in which skeletal disorder characterized by defective mineralization of growing bone?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Rickets is the pediatric manifestation of vitamin D deficiency, causing impaired mineralization of growing bones.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which vitamin functions as a cofactor for gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Vitamin K is essential for the post-translational gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues on clotting factors.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which trace element deficiency is associated with impaired wound healing, hypogonadism, and altered taste (dysgeusia)?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Zinc deficiency impairs wound healing, immune function, growth, and taste sensation.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Iodine deficiency during pregnancy is a leading preventable cause of which condition in the offspring?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Severe maternal iodine deficiency impairs fetal thyroid hormone production, essential for neurodevelopment, causing cretinism.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: The basal metabolic rate (BMR) is best defined as which of the following?
o: Energy expended in digesting food (thermic effect)
Minimum energy required to maintain vital functions at complete rest, post-absorptive state
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: BMR represents the minimal energy needed for basic physiological functions in a resting, fasting, thermoneutral state.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: The thermic effect of food refers to which physiological process?
o: Energy expended in digesting, absorbing, and metabolizing ingested nutrients
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: The thermic effect of food accounts for the energy cost of processing ingested nutrients, typically about 10% of total energy expenditure.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which macronutrient has the highest thermic effect of food (proportion of its energy used in processing)?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Protein has the highest thermic effect, typically 20-30% of its energy content, compared to fats and carbohydrates.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: During prolonged starvation, which fuel source becomes the primary energy substrate for the brain after glycogen stores are depleted?
o: Free fatty acids directly crossing the blood-brain barrier
Ketone bodies derived from fatty acid oxidation
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: After initial glycogen depletion, the brain adapts to use ketone bodies produced from hepatic fatty acid oxidation during prolonged fasting.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which hormone is primarily responsible for promoting glycogen synthesis in the liver and muscle after a meal?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Insulin promotes glycogen synthesis (glycogenesis) via activation of glycogen synthase in the fed state.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which enzyme catalyzes the rate-limiting step of glycogenolysis?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Glycogen phosphorylase catalyzes the rate-limiting cleavage of glucose units from glycogen.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which vitamin acts as a coenzyme in decarboxylation reactions, notably in the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, and its deficiency causes beriberi?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Thiamine pyrophosphate is a critical cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which essential fatty acid deficiency can result from severe fat malabsorption, presenting with dermatitis and impaired wound healing?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Linoleic acid is an essential omega-6 fatty acid; deficiency causes scaly dermatitis and other complications.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Kwashiorkor's characteristic fatty liver results from which underlying biochemical mechanism?
o: Increased hepatic lipogenesis from excess carbohydrate
Impaired synthesis of apolipoproteins needed to export triglycerides as VLDL, due to protein deficiency
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Protein deficiency impairs apolipoprotein synthesis, reducing VLDL export of triglycerides and causing hepatic steatosis.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: The Harris-Benedict equation is used to estimate which physiological parameter?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: The Harris-Benedict equation estimates basal metabolic rate based on weight, height, age, and sex.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Refeeding syndrome, a dangerous complication of reintroducing nutrition after prolonged starvation, is primarily characterized by which electrolyte disturbance?
o: Severe hypophosphatemia (along with hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia)
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Refeeding triggers insulin release, driving phosphate (and potassium, magnesium) intracellularly, causing severe hypophosphatemia.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Body mass index (BMI) is calculated using which formula?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: BMI is defined as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which type of dietary fiber is most associated with slowing gastric emptying and lowering postprandial blood glucose and cholesterol?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Soluble fiber forms a viscous gel that slows gastric emptying and glucose absorption and binds bile acids, lowering cholesterol.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which amino acid, though non-essential in healthy individuals, is considered conditionally essential during illness or metabolic stress?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Glutamine becomes conditionally essential during catabolic states such as critical illness, when demand exceeds endogenous synthesis.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which of the following best describes the biochemical basis of lactose intolerance?
o: Deficiency of brush-border lactase, leading to undigested lactose causing osmotic diarrhea and bacterial fermentation
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Lactase deficiency prevents lactose hydrolysis, leading to osmotic diarrhea and gas production from bacterial fermentation in the colon.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Phenylketonuria (PKU) results from deficiency of which enzyme, requiring dietary restriction of phenylalanine?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: PKU results from phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency, preventing conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine and causing toxic accumulation.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which of the following vitamins requires bile salts and pancreatic lipase for optimal absorption, being fat-soluble?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Vitamin K, like other fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K), requires micellar solubilization via bile salts for absorption.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which condition results from excessive vitamin A intake, presenting with symptoms including headache, hepatotoxicity, and skin changes?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Excess vitamin A intake (hypervitaminosis A) can cause hepatotoxicity, increased intracranial pressure, and skin desquamation.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Folate deficiency during early pregnancy is strongly associated with increased risk of which fetal abnormality?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Adequate folate is essential for neural tube closure; deficiency significantly increases the risk of neural tube defects.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which of the following best describes the metabolic fate of excess dietary carbohydrate beyond immediate energy needs and glycogen storage capacity?
o: Conversion to fatty acids via lipogenesis and storage as triglycerides
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Excess carbohydrate, beyond glycogen storage capacity, is converted to fatty acids via de novo lipogenesis and stored as triglycerides.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Essential trace element copper serves as a cofactor for which enzyme involved in connective tissue cross-linking?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Copper-dependent lysyl oxidase cross-links collagen and elastin fibers, essential for connective tissue strength.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which vitamin's deficiency is specifically linked to a bleeding tendency in newborns, prompting routine prophylactic injection at birth?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Newborns have low vitamin K stores and immature gut flora, prompting routine vitamin K prophylaxis to prevent hemorrhagic disease of the newborn.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which mineral's deficiency is a leading global cause of microcytic hypochromic anemia?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Iron deficiency is the most common cause of microcytic hypochromic anemia worldwide.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: The Atwater factors used to estimate caloric content of foods assign which approximate values (kcal/g) to carbohydrate, protein, and fat respectively?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Standard Atwater conversion factors are approximately 4 kcal/g for carbohydrate and protein, and 9 kcal/g for fat.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which condition results from chronic excessive alcohol intake displacing adequate nutrition, commonly causing thiamine deficiency and Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Chronic alcoholism impairs nutrient intake and absorption, notably thiamine, predisposing to Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which of the following statements about dietary cholesterol and blood cholesterol levels is most accurate?
o: Dietary cholesterol has no relationship whatsoever to blood cholesterol in any individual
Only dietary cholesterol affects blood lipid levels
Blood cholesterol is entirely independent of diet
Saturated and trans fats generally have a greater impact on raising LDL cholesterol than dietary cholesterol itself for most people
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Current understanding emphasizes that saturated and trans fat intake has a larger overall effect on LDL cholesterol than dietary cholesterol alone for most individuals.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which micronutrient deficiency is classically associated with impaired collagen hydroxylation and a bleeding, swollen gum presentation in sailors historically?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Scurvy, from vitamin C deficiency, was historically common among sailors lacking fresh fruit, causing impaired collagen synthesis.

git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.s: Which amino acid is classified as conditionally essential in infants due to limited capacity for its synthesis?
git-and-nutrition/nutrition-and-metaboli.e: Histidine is considered essential in infants and conditionally essential in certain states, given limited endogenous synthetic capacity.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The kidneys are located at which vertebral levels, with the right kidney typically slightly lower than the left?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The kidneys span approximately T12 to L3, with the right kidney positioned slightly lower due to the liver.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which structure is the functional and structural unit of the kidney?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The nephron, consisting of the glomerulus and renal tubule, is the basic functional unit of the kidney.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The renal artery is a direct branch of which vessel?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The renal arteries arise directly from the abdominal aorta at approximately the L1-L2 level.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which kidney's renal vein is typically longer, crossing anterior to the aorta to reach the IVC?
o: The right renal vein crosses posterior to the aorta
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The left renal vein is longer, crossing anterior to the aorta before draining into the IVC, making it vulnerable to compression (nutcracker phenomenon).

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The ureter crosses which structure at the pelvic brim, an important surgical landmark?
o: Bifurcation of the common iliac artery
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The ureter crosses the pelvic brim near the bifurcation of the common iliac artery into external and internal iliac arteries.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which layer of connective tissue directly surrounds the kidney, deep to the perirenal fat?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Gerota's fascia is the renal fascia that encloses the kidney and perirenal fat, separating it from pararenal fat.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The three normal sites of physiological ureteric constriction, relevant to kidney stone impaction, are the pelviureteric junction, pelvic brim, and which third site?
o: At the level of the iliac crest
Where it exits the renal hilum
Where it crosses the bladder wall (vesicoureteric junction)
Where it crosses the psoas muscle
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The vesicoureteric junction, where the ureter enters the bladder obliquely, is a common site for stone impaction.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which structure within the renal hilum is typically most posterior, among the artery, vein, and pelvis?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: From anterior to posterior at the hilum: renal vein, renal artery, then renal pelvis (mnemonic VAP).

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The adrenal (suprarenal) gland receives arterial supply from which three sources?
o: Inferior phrenic artery, aorta directly, and renal artery
Superior mesenteric artery, renal artery, and aorta
Celiac trunk, splenic artery, and renal artery
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The adrenal glands have a rich blood supply from three sources: superior (inferior phrenic artery), middle (aorta), and inferior (renal artery) suprarenal arteries.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The right adrenal vein drains directly into which vessel?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The short right adrenal vein drains directly into the IVC, unlike the longer left adrenal vein which drains into the left renal vein.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which part of the nephron is primarily located within the renal cortex, containing the glomerulus?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The renal corpuscle, comprising the glomerulus and Bowman's capsule, is located in the renal cortex.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The loop of Henle of juxtamedullary nephrons extends deep into which renal region, important for the countercurrent mechanism?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops of Henle extending deep into the medulla, critical for generating the medullary concentration gradient.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The renal papilla empties urine into which structure?
o: Major calyx directly, bypassing minor calyces
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Each renal papilla drains into a minor calyx, which then unites to form major calyces, then the renal pelvis.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which peritoneal relationship best describes the kidneys' position in the abdominal cavity?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The kidneys are retroperitoneal organs, lying posterior to the peritoneum against the posterior abdominal wall.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The male urethra is divided into which parts, from proximal to distal?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The male urethra passes through the prostatic, membranous, and spongy (penile) segments in that order.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which muscle forms the external urethral sphincter, providing voluntary control over urination?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The external urethral sphincter (sphincter urethrae) is skeletal muscle under voluntary somatic control via the pudendal nerve.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The trigone of the bladder is bounded by which three openings?
o: Two ureteric orifices and the apex of the bladder
Two ureteric orifices and the bladder neck vessels
Two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice
Internal and external urethral orifices only
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The trigone is a smooth triangular region bounded by the two ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which nerve provides parasympathetic innervation to the bladder detrusor muscle, promoting micturition?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Parasympathetic fibers via the pelvic splanchnic nerves (S2-S4) stimulate detrusor contraction during micturition.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Sympathetic innervation to the bladder, via the hypogastric nerve, primarily has which effect during the storage phase?
o: Has no effect on bladder function
Contracts the detrusor and relaxes the internal sphincter
Relaxes the detrusor and contracts the internal sphincter (promoting storage)
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Sympathetic stimulation relaxes the detrusor and contracts the internal urethral sphincter, favoring urine storage.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The renal fascia (Gerota's fascia) is important clinically because it can limit the spread of which condition?
o: Perinephric abscess or hematoma to adjacent structures
Urinary tract infection ascending from the bladder
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Gerota's fascia can contain perinephric collections such as abscesses or hematomas, limiting their spread within the retroperitoneum.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which vessel anomaly, a persistent embryological remnant, can cause compression of the ureteropelvic junction, contributing to hydronephrosis?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: An aberrant lower pole renal artery crossing the ureteropelvic junction is a recognized cause of extrinsic obstruction and hydronephrosis.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The female urethra is shorter than the male urethra, contributing to which clinical predisposition?
o: Lower risk of urinary tract infections
Higher risk of ascending urinary tract infections
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The shorter female urethra provides a shorter path for ascending bacteria, predisposing to more frequent UTIs in women.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which structure, a remnant of the fetal allantois, runs from the bladder apex to the umbilicus in adults?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The median umbilical ligament is the fibrous remnant of the urachus, connecting the bladder apex to the umbilicus.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: A patent urachus, if it fails to obliterate completely, can result in which clinical presentation?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: A patent urachus creates an abnormal communication between the bladder and umbilicus, causing urine leakage from the umbilical area.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Horseshoe kidney, a common renal fusion anomaly, is typically caused by fusion of which part of the kidneys and is usually trapped by which structure during ascent?
o: Fusion of the lower poles, trapped beneath the inferior mesenteric artery
Fusion of the lateral borders, trapped by the aorta
Fusion of the lower poles, trapped by the superior mesenteric artery root
Fusion of the upper poles, trapped by the renal artery
No specific trapping structure is involved
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Horseshoe kidney results from fusion of the lower poles; the fused isthmus is typically trapped beneath the root of the inferior mesenteric artery during ascent, so it fails to rotate and ascend fully.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The kidneys receive approximately what percentage of resting cardiac output, reflecting their high metabolic and filtration demands?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The kidneys receive a disproportionately large share (about 20-25%) of resting cardiac output relative to their mass.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which segment of the nephron is primarily located in the renal cortex, situated between the loop of Henle and collecting duct, important for sodium and water reabsorption regulation?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The distal convoluted tubule lies in the cortex and is a key site for regulated sodium and water reabsorption, influenced by aldosterone and ADH-related mechanisms downstream.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The juxtaglomerular apparatus, important in renin secretion and tubuloglomerular feedback, is formed by which two structures in close apposition?
o: Bowman's capsule and efferent arteriole only
Macula densa (distal tubule) and juxtaglomerular cells (afferent arteriole)
Loop of Henle and collecting duct
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The macula densa of the distal tubule and juxtaglomerular (granular) cells of the afferent arteriole together form the juxtaglomerular apparatus.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which structure carries blood away from the glomerulus toward the peritubular capillaries?
o: Vasa recta directly from the aorta
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The efferent arteriole carries blood away from the glomerular capillaries toward the peritubular capillary network.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The vasa recta are specialized capillaries that run parallel to which nephron structure, crucial for the countercurrent exchange mechanism?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Vasa recta parallel the loops of Henle of juxtamedullary nephrons, preserving the medullary osmotic gradient via countercurrent exchange.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Polycystic kidney disease (autosomal dominant form) is most commonly caused by mutation in which gene?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Mutations in PKD1 (and less commonly PKD2) cause the majority of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease cases.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The renal pelvis is continuous distally with which structure?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The renal pelvis narrows and becomes continuous with the ureter as it exits the renal hilum.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which muscle layer of the ureter and bladder wall is responsible for propelling urine via peristalsis?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Smooth muscle in the ureteric wall and the detrusor muscle in the bladder generate peristaltic contractions to propel urine.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The right kidney is typically positioned slightly lower than the left kidney due to which adjacent organ?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The bulk of the liver occupying the right upper quadrant pushes the right kidney slightly inferior to the left.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which vessel, if compressed between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery, causes 'nutcracker syndrome,' presenting with hematuria and flank pain?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Nutcracker syndrome results from compression of the left renal vein between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which congenital anomaly results from the kidney failing to ascend from the pelvis to its normal lumbar position during development?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: An ectopic pelvic kidney results from failure of normal ascent during embryological development.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Duplex (duplicated) collecting systems result from which embryological event?
o: Premature division of the ureteric bud
Fusion of two separate metanephric blastemas
renal/renal-anatomy.e: Early or complete splitting of the ureteric bud results in a duplicated collecting system, sometimes with two separate ureters.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The Weigert-Meyer rule describes the relationship between the insertion points of ureters in a complete duplex system: the upper pole ureter inserts where relative to the lower pole ureter?
o: Inferior and medial (upper pole ureter inserts lower and more medially)
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The Weigert-Meyer rule states the upper pole ureter inserts inferomedially (often ectopically), while the lower pole ureter inserts superolaterally, predisposing to reflux.

renal/renal-anatomy.s: Which structure marks the point where the ureter is most likely to be injured during pelvic or gynecological surgery, due to its proximity to the uterine artery?
o: Where the ureter passes under the uterine artery ('water under the bridge')
Where the ureter exits the kidney
Where the ureter crosses the common iliac artery
Where the ureter enters the bladder
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The ureter passes just beneath the uterine artery near the cervix, a classic site of iatrogenic injury during hysterectomy ('water under the bridge').

renal/renal-anatomy.s: The suprarenal (adrenal) glands are enclosed within which fascial layer, shared with the kidney?
renal/renal-anatomy.e: The adrenal glands share the renal (Gerota's) fascial envelope with the kidneys, though a thin septum separates them.

renal/renal-physiology-filtration-reabso.s: Glomerular filtration rate (GFR) is best defined as which of the following?
o: Volume of plasma filtered by the glomeruli per unit time
Amount of a substance reabsorbed by the tubules
Volume of blood filtered by both kidneys per day exactly equal to cardiac output
Volume of urine excreted per day
Total renal blood flow per minute
renal/renal-physiology-filtration-reabso.e: GFR is the volume of plasma filtered across the glomerular capillaries into Bowman's space per unit time, normally about 120 mL/min.

renal/renal-physiology-filtration-reabso.s: Which of the following substances is used clinically to estimate GFR because it is freely filtered, not reabsorbed, and only minimally secreted?
renal/renal-physiology-filtration-reabso.e: Creatinine clearance approximates GFR since creatinine is freely filtered and undergoes minimal tubular reabsorption, though some secretion causes slight overestimation.

renal/renal-physiology-filtration-reabso.s: Inulin is considered the gold standard marker for measuring GFR because it is handled by the kidney in which way?
o: Freely filtered, not reabsorbed, not secreted, not metabolized
renal/renal-physiology-filtration-reabso.e: Inulin's filtration without reabsorption, secretion, or metabolism makes its clearance an exact measure of GFR.

renal/renal-physiology-filtration-reabso.s: Which starling force favors filtration at the glomerular capillary?
